title: Hopper FP8 scaler safeguards and calibration oracle for E4M3/E5M2
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
We are preparing to enable FP8 quantization (E4M3/E5M2) across a subset of Hopper-backed models. Recent canary runs surfaced two classes of instability: 1) per-layer scaler oscillation under distributional shift, and 2) calibration drift that causes occasional >1.5% relative generation-quality regressions on long-tail prompts.

Goal:
Design and implement a low-risk activation path that pairs: (A) a lightweight on-device "scaler safeguard" that detects and corrects unstable per-tensor exponent scaling, and (B) a calibration oracle service that validates candidate quantization profiles against a canonical prompt corpus and live-shadow telemetry before promotion. The feature should allow safe canary → staged rollout with automated rollback triggers.

Scope / Non-goals:
- In-scope: runtime scaler hysteresis, per-batch stability guard, calibration oracle API, CI validation harness updates, dashboarding/alerts, canary gating rules.
- Out-of-scope: full INT8 profiling, model re-training, compiler-level kernel rewrites (may be follow-ups).

Design summary:
1) Scaler Safeguard: implement hysteresis on FP8 exponent updates with three buckets (stable, watch, emergency) decided by recent variance and peak absolute accumulation across recent batches. On "watch" we clamp update step-size; on "emergency" we fallback to stored EMA FP8 profile derived from the last known-good calibration. All changes are per-layer and recorded in telemetry.
2) Calibration Oracle: service that runs candidate profiles through: (a) deterministic calibration suite (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/QP/FP8+Calibration+Suite), (b) a stochastic prompt holdout matching production distributions, and (c) a lightweight generation-quality check using embedding-based similarity + token-level delta thresholds. Oracle outputs pass/fail and a graded stability score.
3) Canary gating: combine oracle pass + real-time telemetry gates (error rate, hallucination-signal, token-diff percentiles) to decide promotion. If telemetry breaches thresholds, automated rollback via runtime policy will switch traffic to float or INT8 fallback.

Acceptance criteria:
- Scaler safeguard implemented in runtime and covered by unit + integration tests.
- Calibration oracle implemented and wired to CI so every candidate profile runs through it automatically.
- Canary pipeline enforces oracle pass + live telemetry gating before promoting a profile to staged rollout.
- No run-level generation-quality regressions >1.0% for any canary job across the canonical prompt set; emergency rollback occurs automatically if 1.5% regressions are observed.
- Observability: dashboard tile showing per-layer scaler variance, oracle score distribution, canary pass/fail history.

Telemetry & KPIs:
- Per-layer scaler variance (p95/p99) tracked. Target: reduce emergency-trigger rate to <0.1% of inferences for canary traffic.
- Calibration oracle false-positive rate <5% on historical candidates.
- Canary generation-quality regressions >1.5% must trigger rollback within 5 minutes.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement runtime safeguard behind a feature flag; unit tests and local simulation harness.
2) Deploy to internal canary fleet (10% of canary nodes) for 48h with shadow mode telemetry.
3) Enable calibration oracle in CI and run against stored candidate profiles; tune thresholds.
4) Open staged rollout to 1% production for two stable models with automatic rollback.
5) Observe for 7 days, expand to more models incrementally.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: safeguard introduces latency regressions. Mitigation: microbenchmark and ensure <1ms p95 added per-request; implement as asynchronous correction where possible.
- Risk: oracle overfits canonical corpus. Mitigation: include live-shadow prompt samples and random holdouts; rotate corpus monthly.

Deliverables & artifacts:
- Runtime change PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2148
- Calibration oracle repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/calibration-oracle/tree/feat/hopper-fp8
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/QP/Hopper+FP8+Scaler+Safeguard+Design

Notes:
Keep the default behavior conservative: prefer false negatives (rejecting a safe profile) to false positives (promoting an unstable profile). The rollout policy must allow a human-in-the-loop approval for first two production model families.

2025-02-18 - Marcus: Implemented hysteresis buckets and local unit tests. PR opened (runtime): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2148. Benchmarks show +0.5ms p95 on 1k token sequences.

2025-02-21 - Priya Kaur (review): Suggested tightening emergency threshold and adding an opt-out annotation per-model to skip safeguard for low-latency critical routes. Approved changes pending telemetry dashboard updates.

2025-02-25 - Marcus: Calibration oracle MVP wired into CI. First candidate runs show oracle score correlates with manual evals (Spearman rho=0.72). Added canary gating rule to require oracle_score>=0.8.
2025-03-02 - SRE (Tom): Canary run observed two rollback events in 24h tied to long-tail prompts; added log-sampling for failing traces and created incident follow-up ENG-100210 to deep-dive.
acceptance_criteria: 1) runtime safeguard behind flag with tests; 2) calibration oracle in CI; 3) canary gating enforces oracle + telemetry; 4) automated rollback triggers at 1.5% regression; 5) observability dashboard in Console showing per-layer metrics
notes: Prefer conservative activation. If runtime safeguard interacts with existing quant fallback flows, coordinate with Compiler and Serving runtime owners. Use feature flag naming: fp8_scaler_safeguard_v1.
